cohort: The study included 28 rhesus macaque fetuses (14 EtOH exposed and 14 controls) generated from dams that self-administered ethanol or isocaloric maltose dextrin prior to and through the first 60 days of a 168-day gestation term.
finding: Daily 1.5 g/kg EtOH exposure through the first trimester in rhesus macaques did not influence pregnancy success rates or cause gross adverse effects on pregnancy, but pregnancy did influence the dams' drinking behavior during the second month of gestation.
gest_age: Fetuses were delivered by caesarean section at G85, G110, or G135 of a 168-day gestation.
